title: Shuffle Squares in Differentiable Words
summary: Experiments on binary run-length differentiability lead to sharp computer-assisted criteria for shuffle squares. Every $C^3$-word of length greater than $16$ is a shuffle square exactly when both letter multiplicities are even. All $34$ nonempty even-Parikh exceptions are smooth and persist in every higher differentiability class. For $C^2$ the sharp threshold is $48$, with $212$ nonempty exceptions.
